why.text: Granite soils in a region ringed by mountains that shelter it from wet coastal air and harsh winds, with cold, rainy winters and hot summers.

styles.text: Reds, whites and rosados, plus sparkling wines.

climate.text: Temperate: cold and rainy in winter, very hot and dry in summer. Mountains block damp coastal air and harsh continental winds, and the relief creates marked microclimate variations.

soil.text: Mostly granite, with brown non-humic lithosols and a few brown Mediterranean schist outcrops. The soils weather easily, which suits vines.

tastes.text: Reds: ruby, full-bodied, delicate, soft and velvety with age. Whites: light, fresh, citrus-yellow, fruity. Rosés: fresh, simple fruit with some floral notes. Sparkling: fine persistent bubbles, fruity and fresh.

styles.name: Nobre
styles.text: Minimum alcohol 12% red and rosado, 11.5% white. Ageing: red 36 months, white 12.

styles.name: Garrafeira
styles.text: Red needs 36 months ageing, 12 in bottle. White needs 12 months, 6 in bottle.

styles.name: Reserva
styles.text: Red needs 24 months ageing. White needs 6 months.

styles.name: Clarete
styles.text: Red wine with a minimum of 6 months ageing.

why.text: Clay and clay-limestone hills under a strong Atlantic influence, with hot days and cool nights in summer; the sea shows in fresh acidity.

styles.text: Red, white and rosado wines, plus sparkling wine made by the classic bottle method.

climate.text: Mediterranean/Atlantic climate with hot-day, cool-night summers; the Atlantic Ocean to the west gives strong maritime influence and fresh acidity.

soil.text: Mostly poor mineral soils from sandy to clayey, and some sandy loam; vines grow mainly on clay and clay-limestone. The best reds come from clay-limestone with south exposure and good drainage.

tastes.text: Reds: structured by tannin and alcohol, with blackberry, bergamot and spice when young, and long ageing. Whites: pale lemon, fresh, floral or fruity. Rosés: fruity, with fairly high acidity. Sparkling: fresh and fruity, toasty with age.

styles.name: Clássico
styles.text: Red with at least 50% Baga and at least 12.5% natural alcohol.

styles.name: Espumante
styles.text: Sparkling wine with second fermentation in bottle (classic method), nine months ageing before sale.

styles.name: Reserva
styles.text: Traditional quality mention the spec lists, along with Superior and Super reserva.

styles.name: Garrafeira
styles.text: Traditional quality mention the spec lists, along with Escolha and Colheita Seleccionada.

why.text: Vineyards at 300 to 700 m on schist, gneiss and granite, with a dry Mediterranean summer, give fresh, aromatic whites and spicy reds.

styles.text: Reds (including palhete and clarete), whites and rosados, plus sparkling wine.

climate.text: Mediterranean climate with 800 to 1000 mm of rain a year, mostly in winter and spring. Summers are very dry, with under 10 mm in July and August.

soil.text: Brown or red Mediterranean soils on schist and gneiss, brown soils on schist or greywacke, and stony non-humic soils on granite and migmatite.

tastes.text: Whites: very aromatic and fresh. Reds: more complex, with spice and red fruit aromas and great freshness. Sparkling: fresh and very aromatic.

styles.name: Selecção
styles.text: Red needs at least 13% alcohol and 12 months ageing; white 12% and six months.

styles.name: Palhete
styles.text: Red from partial skin contact or red and white grapes, whites at most 15%.

styles.name: Clarete
styles.text: Red made like palhete, white grapes up to 45%, 11.5% alcohol at most.

styles.name: Espumante
styles.text: Sparkling wine, at least 11% alcohol and nine months at the producer after bottling.

why.text: Terraced vineyards along the Vouga valley on schist, gneiss, granite and migmatite soils; the whites are low-alcohol, fruity and rich in malic acid.

styles.text: Still white and red wines; both may show a light prickle of gas.

soil.text: Humic lithosols on sedimentary and metamorphosed schist, gneiss, granite and migmatite.

tastes.text: Whites: lemon to light gold, very aromatic, fruity, tangy, rich in malic acid, sometimes slightly sparkling. Reds: ruby to violet, aromatic, tangy, some astringency, high fixed acidity, long ageing, sometimes slightly sparkling.

styles.name: Reserva
styles.text: Traditional label mention allowed for Lafões wines; the spec gives no further rule.

styles.name: Garrafeira
styles.text: Traditional label mention allowed for Lafões wines; the spec gives no further rule.

styles.name: Superior
styles.text: Traditional label mention allowed for Lafões wines; the spec gives no further rule.

styles.name: Escolha
styles.text: Traditional label mention allowed for Lafões wines; the spec gives no further rule.

why.text: Vineyards on the slopes of the Serra de Aire between the coast and the limestone massif, with a mild climate and very varied soils.

styles.text: Red, white and rosé wines, including the Medieval de Ourém white and red.

climate.text: Mild climate with microclimates, seen as a transition between the wet western winds and dry summers.

soil.text: Very varied: brown or red limestone soils on marl and fine sandstone, Mediterranean soils on sandstone and clay, and non-humic lithosols and podzols on sandstone.

tastes.text: Reds: light, open ruby, sometimes fruity, soft quality tannins. Rosés: balanced, fruity, some freshness. Whites: light, soft, fruity, deep yellow, with some persistence.

styles.name: Medieval de Ourém
styles.text: Ourém wines made by medieval, Cistercian-monk methods, yield capped at 40 hl per hectare.
